title: Button + LED
summary: Now let's synthesize inputs and outputs together!

steps.title: Button + LED

quickCheck.question: Why must an external LED have a resistor in series when driven by an Arduino digital pin?
options: To limit electric current and protect both the LED semiconductor and Arduino pin from burning out
To change the color of the emitted light
To convert direct current into alternating current
quickCheck.explanation: LEDs have negligible internal resistance; a series resistor prevents destructive overcurrent.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Remember from Lesson 4: LEDs draw excessive current unless protected by a current-limiting resistor.

quickCheck.question: How do you invert your code so the LED stays ON normally and turns OFF only when the button is held?
options: Change the condition to write HIGH when buttonState == HIGH, and LOW when buttonState == LOW
Reverse the power wires on the Arduino Uno
Change the baud rate in Serial.begin()
quickCheck.explanation: Flipping the conditional logic in code inverts how the output responds to the physical input state.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Software logic controls the relationship: flipping your `if-else` branch reverses the action.
